title: What Is The Gospel
paragraphs: Understanding "The Gospel": The Good News of Jesus Christ

The word gospel literally means "good news." At the heart of the Christian faith, the gospel is the message of God's saving work accomplished through Jesus Christ. This message is foundational to the Bible and is central to both personal salvation and the mission of the church.
1. The Gospel: God’s Initiative Towards Humanity

From the beginning, Scripture teaches that all people have sinned and fallen short of God's glory (Romans 3:23). Sin separates humanity from God, resulting in spiritual death (Romans 6:23). However, the gospel proclaims God's initiative to rescue and redeem:
"For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him shall not perish but have eternal life." (John 3:16 NIV)
The gospel begins with God's love for a lost world. He sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to bring salvation.
2. The Gospel: The Person and Work of Jesus Christ
The gospel centers on the life, death, and resurrection of Jesus:

"For what I received I passed on to you as of first importance: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures..." (1 Corinthians 15:3-4 NIV)

Jesus, fully God and fully man (John 1:1-14), lived a sinless life and willingly died as a substitutionary sacrifice for sinners. He took the punishment for our sins upon Himself, satisfying God’s justice. His resurrection proved His victory over sin and death, affirming His divine identity and the truth of His promises.
3. The Gospel: Salvation by Grace Through Faith
The response the gospel calls for is not human effort, but faith in Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior. Salvation is a free gift of God's grace, not something earned:
"For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God—not by works, so that no one can boast." (Ephesians 2:8-9 NIV)
By trusting in Jesus—turning from sin and believing in His finished work—anyone can receive forgiveness and eternal life.
4. The Gospel: Transformation and Hope

The gospel not only brings forgiveness, but transforms lives. Believers are given a new heart, the indwelling Holy Spirit, and a new purpose to live for Christ and share His message (2 Corinthians 5:17-21). The gospel also gives hope for the future, promising eternal life with God.
"For I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God that brings salvation to everyone who believes: first to the Jew, then to the Gentile." (Romans 1:16 NIV)
5. The Gospel: A Message for All
The gospel is intended for all peoples, regardless of background or past. Jesus commands His followers to proclaim this good news to the whole world (Matthew 28:18-20).
Summary

The gospel is the good news that, through Jesus Christ, God has provided a way for sinners to be reconciled to Himself, forgiven, and given new life—now and forever. It is received by faith alone, and it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes.
